reference.source: Fitzpatrick's Dermatology / Rook's Textbook of Dermatology
clinicalPearls: A chronic, recurrent, inflammatory disease of the apocrine-gland-bearing flexures: axillae, groin, perineum, buttocks, and inframammary folds
Presents with painful, deep-seated inflammatory nodules, abscesses, discharging sinus tracts, and eventually rope-like scarring
Double-ended (bridged) comedones in affected areas are a helpful diagnostic clue
It is a primarily inflammatory, not infective, disease, though secondary bacterial colonisation and infection occur; recurrent painful lesions in typical sites over time define it
Strongly associated with obesity, smoking, and metabolic syndrome, and weight loss and smoking cessation are important management measures
Severity guides treatment: topical and oral antibacterials for anti-inflammatory effect in milder disease, and biologic immunomodulators, hormonal therapy, or surgery for moderate to severe disease
Definitive control of extensive or recurrent disease often requires wide surgical excision of affected tissue rather than incision and drainage alone
The condition causes considerable pain, malodour, and psychological distress, and quality of life should be actively assessed
reference.pathophysiology: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic inflammatory disorder centred on the hair follicle in apocrine-bearing skin. The primary event is follicular occlusion by hyperkeratosis, leading to follicular dilatation, rupture, and release of keratin and bacteria into the surrounding dermis. This provokes an intense inflammatory response with nodules and abscesses; recurrent inflammation drives formation of epithelialised sinus tracts and progressive scarring. Genetic predisposition, dysregulated innate immunity, hormonal influences, obesity, and smoking all contribute. Although bacteria colonise lesions and secondary infection occurs, the disease is fundamentally inflammatory rather than a primary infection.
additionalDifferentials: Crohn's disease with cutaneous or perianal involvement
Cutaneous tuberculosis or actinomycosis in atypical sinus-forming disease
Lymphogranuloma venereum in the anogenital region
additionalInvestigations: Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic lesions, sites, and recurrence
Bacterial swabs of discharging lesions when secondary infection is suspected
Imaging such as ultrasound or MRI to map sinus tracts before surgery in extensive disease
Screening for associated metabolic disease, including glucose and lipids
Assessment for inflammatory bowel disease when gastrointestinal symptoms coexist
redFlags: Severe systemic infection or sepsis arising from deep abscesses
Long-standing chronic sinuses with new induration or non-healing ulceration, raising concern for squamous cell carcinoma
Extensive scarring causing contractures or restricted limb movement
Severe unremitting pain and profound impairment of quality of life
reference.prognosis: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic, often progressive disease with a relapsing course; early recognition and treatment can limit scarring, but advanced disease causes substantial morbidity, and long-standing lesions carry a small risk of malignant transformation.
pitfalls: Repeatedly treating flares as simple abscesses with incision and drainage while missing the underlying chronic disease
Relying solely on antibacterials and overlooking the inflammatory nature requiring anti-inflammatory or surgical management
Neglecting smoking cessation and weight management as core interventions
Failing to consider squamous cell carcinoma in chronic non-healing lesions
management: Smoking cessation and weight reduction as disease-modifying lifestyle measures
Topical or oral antibacterials (topical clindamycin, oral tetracyclines) for their anti-inflammatory effect in milder disease
Biologic immunomodulators such as TNF-alpha inhibitors (adalimumab) or IL-17 inhibitors for moderate-to-severe disease
Hormonal therapy with anti-androgens or a combined oral contraceptive in appropriate women
Acute flare control with intralesional corticosteroid and incision and drainage of painful abscesses
Wide surgical excision or deroofing of persistent epithelialised sinus tracts in refractory or advanced disease
Pain management, psychological support, and screening for and treatment of associated metabolic syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease
